dedupe_keys.name: a global dataset of spatiotemporal drought events from reanalysis and hydrological model data for 1980 2024

description: A global dataset of spatiotemporal drought events from reanalysis and hydrological model data for 1980–2024 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Vít Šťovíček et al. We present a global dataset of spatiotemporally clustered drought events for 1980–2024, derived from daily precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, soil moisture, and surface runoff data. Drought conditions were consistently defined using a 10th percentile threshold and clustered in space and time using a three–dimensional implementation of the Density–Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm. Coverage: global; published in 2026. Formats: NetCDF, Image. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support communication-network and digital-infrastructure studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
